segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: What was to speak in Spanish?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Hablé. And he spoke, she spoke, you formal spoke?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Habló, good. We spoke is hablamos, which, I'm sure you've noticed, is exactly the same as the present we speak.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So hablamos means we speak or we spoke, which for one side is wonderful because it means you get another version of this very irregular tense without having to to remember a new one, but of course it can cause some ambiguity and in real life it can cause some ambiguity, not often, mind, because most of the time you have some context showing that you're talking about the past.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: For example, the word for when is cuándo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So if you want to say when we speak, I understand everything. What was to understand?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Comprender. So, when we speak, I understand everything.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Cuando hablamos, comprendo todo. So cuando hablamos, that bit could be when we speak generally, or when we spoke. So that second half brings us into the context and we understand that when we speak, generally speaking, I understand everything: cuando hablamos, comprendo todo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: But if you wanted to say when we spoke, I understood everything, then of course the first bit is going to be the same, but that second bit, I understood everything, is going to give you that context. So let's practice that one: when we spoke, I understood everything.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. Cuando hablamos, comprendí todo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So again, the second part of that sentence is making it clear whether this hablamos is the present or the past: cuando hablamos, comprendo todo; cuando hablamos, comprendí todo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We spoke yesterday. We spoke yesterday.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Hablamos ayer, good. And we know that we can use the present with future context in Spanish. So if you wanted to say we will speak tomorrow:

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Hablamos mañana. So hablamos ayer, we spoke yesterday; hablamos mañana, we will speak tomorrow.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would you say we wait a lot, we wait a lot generally? What is a lot in Spanish?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. To wait or to hope?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Esperar. If you forget this one you can think of desperate, which means unhoped, desesperado in Spanish. Again, one of these -ado / -ido adjectives from the version that comes after haber, you can see desesperar, desesperado, which made desperate. And it's desesperado in Spanish, not desperado. Like we have some Spanishisms, let's say, that have entered English, but they can enter incorrectly, like desperado is desesperado in Spanish. Or in English you might hear 'no problemo'. This is loosely based on Spanish, but of course problem in Spanish is problema, not problemo, and actually you would say ningún problema, not no problema.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So esperar, to wait or to hope. So talking generally: we wait a lot, we wait around a lot:

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Esperamos mucho. Maybe you meant yesterday, no? Here it might be ambiguous unless the context is clear, so if you want to clarify, you might want to say the word yesterday. How how would you say we waited a lot yesterday?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Esperamos mucho ayer. What was to eat?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Comer. And what is we eat?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Comemos. We ate is comimos. Comimos. We ate?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: No comimos. What was to live?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Vivimos. So what this means is that because of this one difference we have in the entire language between -er and -ir verbs: in the present we have -emos for -er and -imos for -ir. What that means is that when we go into the past, -ir verbs stay the same (vivimos, vivimos), but -er verbs are different (comemos, comimos).

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And we see, in the present?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Vimos, good. What was to go out or to leave?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. We're going out or we're leaving?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. And we went out or we left?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: The same. What was to lose?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. How would you say we got lost, or we lost ourselves?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Nos perdimos, good. Okay, so how would you say we always get lost, but we didn't get lost yesterday? First thing, what was the word for always?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Siempre. So how would you say we always get lost?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Siempre nos perdemos, or nos perdemos siempre. But...

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: No perdimos... ah. No nos perdimos ayer.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Nos perdemos siempre, pero no nos perdimos ayer. Very good. There we see in that sentence perdemos for present and perdimos for past. But of course with -ir verbs, they have the same version for both. So we could say, for example, we don't go out often, but we went out yesterday. And often is a menudo. A menudo.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Menudo is like a literary word that's not used very often for small, related to minute actually, or minuscule. It's not used very often in that sense, in the sense of small, but a menudo is used very often to mean often, ah? So, we don't go out often:

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Very good. So here we have the present and the past in this sentence and we see that both of them are salimos. No salimos a menudo, pero salimos ayer.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Let's make a recap. So let's do it with hablar and comer, which we will use as our hook verbs. So I spoke?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And comer is to eat, so I ate?
